bio.value: Brendan F. Boyle represents Pennsylvania's 2nd Congressional District in the U.S. House of Representatives. A Philadelphia native, he earned degrees from the University of Notre Dame and the Harvard Kennedy School. He was elected to the Pennsylvania House of Representatives in 2008 and to the U.S. House in 2014. He serves as the ranking member of the House Budget Committee. His stated priorities include protecting Social Security and Medicare, expanding access to health care, and supporting working families and veterans.

bio.value: Jessica Arriaga is the Republican candidate for Pennsylvania's 2nd Congressional District. A North Philadelphia native, she describes herself as a health-care professional and entrepreneur. Her campaign says she has worked more than 20 years as an operating-room technician and in medical sales and health-care coordination. She says she is running to bring accountability and practical problem-solving to Congress, telling voters she answers 'to the people, period' and is running 'not to talk, but to fix what isn't working and fight for a city that works for you again.'

bio.value: Christopher M. Rabb is the Democratic candidate for Pennsylvania's 3rd Congressional District. He has represented the 200th District in the Pennsylvania House of Representatives since first being elected in 2016, serving five terms. His campaign says he is running 'because it is time to put community over commerce, expand democracy, strengthen workers' rights, guarantee access to healthcare, housing, clean air and water.' He won the May 19, 2026 Democratic primary. The seat is open because incumbent Dwight Evans did not seek reelection.

bio.value: Dennis Mahoney is an independent candidate for Pennsylvania's 3rd Congressional District. His campaign says he has built a career convening businesses, nonprofits, faith communities, and civic leaders to solve problems, shaped by years in disaster relief and long-term development work. In Philadelphia he says he builds coalitions to keep children out of the foster care system, brings neighborhood food markets to food deserts, and partners with the school district to support students and teachers. He founded AOI Solutions. Endorsed by the Forward Party in September 2026, his campaign says he submitted 19,000 petition signatures to earn ballot access.

bio.value: Mary Gay Scanlon has represented Pennsylvania's 5th Congressional District in the U.S. House since 2018. She earned a bachelor's degree from Colgate University and a law degree from the University of Pennsylvania Law School. Before Congress she served as national pro bono counsel at a major law firm, represented the Education Law Center, and served as president of the Wallingford-Swarthmore school board. Her stated priorities include protecting voting rights and democracy, expanding access to health care, and supporting public education and gun-violence prevention.

His campaign website is joshshapiro.org.

bio.value: Ken Krawchuk is the Libertarian nominee for governor of Pennsylvania. He founded an IT consulting firm and describes himself as a business architect for the pharmaceutical, insurance, and financial markets. He has run for governor before and is the only third-party candidate on the November ballot. His campaign says he has 'a solid plan to improve education and cut taxes, including the much-hated property tax,' and favors privatizing public schools, vetoing tax increases, and eliminating school property taxes.

bio.value: Stacy Garrity is the Republican nominee for governor of Pennsylvania. A Bradford County native, she is a retired Army Reserve colonel with three deployments who earned two Bronze Stars and the Legion of Merit. She worked as an accountant and rose to become the first female vice president at Global Tungsten & Powders. Elected Pennsylvania treasurer in 2020 and reelected in 2024, her campaign says she has focused on cutting waste, eliminating taxpayer abuse, and bringing transparency to state government, and has returned more than $1 billion in unclaimed property.

neutral_summary.value: The measure would amend Philadelphia's Home Rule Charter to establish Creative Philadelphia, a city office headed by a Chief Cultural Officer that promotes the city's arts, culture, and creative-economy sector, and to define the office's functions. City Council enacted the submission legislation (Bill No. 260264-A, Resolution No. 260270, approved June 11, 2026) directing that the question appear on the November 3, 2026 ballot.

title.note: Question text from the enacted certified ordinance attachment; official ballot-title formatting from a general-election sample ballot was not located.
title.value: Shall the Philadelphia Home Rule Charter be amended to establish and define the functions of Creative Philadelphia, an office headed by the Chief Cultural Officer to promote the City's arts, culture, and creative economy sector?

what_a_no_means.value: A NO vote would leave the Home Rule Charter unchanged and would not establish Creative Philadelphia.

what_a_yes_means.value: A YES vote would amend the Home Rule Charter to establish Creative Philadelphia, an office headed by the Chief Cultural Officer, and define its functions.

ballot_status.note: Enacted companion ordinance (Bill No. 260459, passed June 4 and signed June 23, 2026) takes effect only upon voter approval, indicating a related ballot question. The final certified ballot-submission ordinance for Bill No. 260457 was not located, and no official general-election sample ballot was found as of 2026-09-28, so status is 'projected', not certified.

full_text_url.note: Final certified full text of the ballot measure not located; the companion enabling ordinance is an official city attachment but not the measure text itself.

neutral_summary.value: The measure would amend the Philadelphia Home Rule Charter's contracting procedures to add a 2% bid preference for businesses certified as both local and small, adjust existing local bid preferences and reporting and goal provisions, and give the Procurement Department and the City Solicitor discretion over bond requirements for certain construction projects. The related ordinance (Bill No. 260459, signed June 23, 2026) takes effect only upon voter approval of the ballot question.

title.note: Final certified ballot question text not located. The draft ballot-submission bill (Bill No. 260457) contains drafting artifacts ('increase modify') and placeholders, so its text is not used as the title. BallotReady lists it as 'Expanding Small Business Contracting Opportunities' (unofficial display title).

what_a_no_means.value: A NO vote would leave the Charter's contracting procedures unchanged, and the companion ordinance adding a 2% bid preference for certified local and small businesses would not take effect.

what_a_yes_means.value: A YES vote would amend the Charter's contracting procedures to add a 2% bid preference for businesses certified as both local and small, and the companion ordinance revising contracting rules would take effect.
